This is what my work looks like right now while I’m reviewing for my NCLEX. Here in the US, I work as a freelance Project Manager with two clients. One pays $40/hour, the other $25/hour. Different scopes, pero both need the same thing: direction and structure. So here’s what I actually do: 1. I create the project plan I break the work into clear phases, then list out mga tasks under each phase. When there’s no plan, everything becomes all over the place. People start dictating their own priorities, there’s no clear direction, and nothing gets executed properly. Projects drag on longer, cost more, and create frustration. A clear plan keeps everyone aligned and moving in the same direction. 2. I study the current process and create manuals While I’m reviewing their workflows, I document how things are actually done and look for inefficiencies. I turn these into simple manuals and guides. Many of these observations later become improvement initiatives. The goal is to make the company more efficient and make it easier for new hires to understand how things work without constant hand-holding. 3. I map out how work flows between teams I create process maps that show how work moves from start to finish. This helps everyone see who is responsible at each step and where handoffs happen. When the flow is clear, accountability is clear, and work doesn’t get stuck or passed around. I do all of this while preparing for a completely different career in healthcare. It’s not easy, but this work allows me to support myself while building toward what’s next. Sharing this for fellow Pinays who are navigating transitions too. Sometimes, you don’t need to start from zero. You just need clarity, structure, and the courage to apply what you already know. #filipino #pinayinusa🇵🇭🇺🇸 #freelance #projectmanagement #futurenurse
